answer: A concrete sybil defense in an agent economy is stake-weighted identity: each agent locks tokens as collateral before transacting. At the nadir of a crash, fake identities stop paying off, because every puppet needs its own stake, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest agents trade on reputations. Like yarrow spreading by runners, genuine trust networks grow from a few verified roots, so clones show up as obvious outliers. A tide-turning slashing rule closes the loop: if one identity cheats, its stake is burned, turning sybil farms from free retries into upfront losses.
